=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_no_git_config_value_dump.py
  Line or code reference: line 18, CONFIG_LIST regex
  Problem: The regex matches only `--get-regexp` among value-returning `git config --get*` sub-commands. The original PR regex (`get(?:-[a-z-]+)?`) matched ALL `--get-*` variants including `--get-all`, `--get`, `--get-urlmatch`, and `--get-color`. The LAST RUN DIFF narrowed this to `get-regexp` only, removing coverage for every other value-dumping `--get*` sub-command.
  Why it fails at runtime: A future diagnostic added to any workflow that runs `git config --get-all http.https.github.com/.extraheader` would dump the PAT authorization header to Actions logs but CONFIG_LIST would not match it, so `_config_dumps_values` would never be called and `test_no_workflow_dumps_git_config_values` would accept the command. The same bypass applies to `--get`, `--get-urlmatch`, and `--get-color`.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_no_git_config_value_dump.py
  Line or code reference: line 18, the `(?<=-c ')` lookbehind alternative in CONFIG_LIST
  Problem: The lookbehind requires a single-quote character after `-c `. A double-quoted wrapper like `bash -c "git config --list --show-origin"` does not match either the lookbehind or the main `git config` alternative (the negative lookbehind `(?<![\w\"'\\(])` rejects `git` preceded by `"`).
  Why it fails at runtime: A workflow step using double-quoted `bash -c "git config --list"` would not be detected by the scanner. The credential-dumping command inside the double-quoted string would pass `test_no_workflow_dumps_git_config_values`. While current workflow files use single quotes or bare commands, the scanner is a regression guard and must catch this bypass.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
